fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled EXIF blob from the image is passed to libexif for parsing; length is the full blob size.

fine_trace.code: const unsigned char *d = d_orig; unsigned int len, fullds;
fine_trace.note: d points to the start of the EXIF blob and ds is its size; both are attacker-controlled.
If the blob does not start with the EXIF header, the APP1 marker search path is taken; d is advanced through JPEG markers.
The loop skips 0xff fill bytes and advances d/ds; attacker controls the byte pattern to drive d past the intended bounds.
For an APPn marker, d is advanced by 1 and ds decremented; then d[0] and d[1] are read to get the segment length l.

fine_trace.code: if (l > ds) return; d += l; ds -= l; continue;
fine_trace.note: The segment length l is attacker-controlled; if l <= ds, d is advanced by l and ds reduced, continuing the loop.
After finding APP1, d is advanced past the marker and length field; ds is reduced accordingly.
The check ds < 6 is intended to protect the 6-byte memcmp, but the attacker can craft the APP1 length so that ds is exactly 6 while d points near the end of the heap buffer.
Heap-buffer-overflow READ of 6 bytes occurs here when d points within 6 bytes of the end of the allocated buffer but ds is reported as >= 6 due to the crafted APP1 length field.
